transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Imani (Redwood CSM), Tom (CTO, Stratus), Priya (Head of ML), Alex (Infra), Sara (Security), Ben (Product)
Shared artifacts: Stratus playbook draft (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/stratus-playbook), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/stratus-tokensec.xlsx)

00:00 - Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm maya, i'm the ae on the account, with daniel our se. hi all.
00:18 - Tom (Stratus): hey, thanks. we'll keep this high level, we want to validate latency/cost tradeoffs for patient-facing summarization flows.
00:35 - Daniel (Redwood): awesome, can you share the primary SLOs? like p95 target and concurrency envelope?
00:42 - Priya (Stratus): yeah, so for short patient-facing replies (<= 128 tokens) we want p95 under 400ms if possible. for long summaries (~512-1k tokens) we care more about steady token/sec streaming — target ~1k tokens/sec aggregated across pool.
01:05 - Maya: got it. and concurrency? peak users?
01:10 - Ben (Product): peak concurrent inference calls about 150, typical 40-70. burst to 250 during morning rounds.
01:20 - Alex (Infra): and network: we're on GCP us-west2, need private connectivity, so VPC peering or Dedicated with egress constraints is important.
01:35 - Sara (Security): additionally we'll need KMS/HSM support, SOC2 docs, and strict audit logs. can't have keys leave our control.
01:47 - Daniel: that's fine — Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and on-prem variants, but there's different cost/latency tradeoffs vs Hosted. for the p95 400ms, do you mean end-to-end including network RTT to your VPC?
02:05 - Priya: yes, end-to-end, from our application to the response finish on stream.
02:12 - Daniel: ok, so we need to model both service-side token generation latency and client-network RTT. in Hosted we can hit lower raw compute latency but network egress and data residency can be a blocker. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower multi-tenant jitter, Private (VPC) gives you data controls but adds some network hops.
02:40 - Tom: any ballparks on token/sec we should expect per-GPU?
02:47 - Daniel: depends on model and quantization. rough order: modern 70B-ish quantized can do ~800-3k tokens/sec depending on sequence length and batch profile; smaller 13B cores can exceed that per-GPU. but the important bit is aggregate across pool + KV cache warm hit rate.
03:05 - Priya: KV cache warm/cold—if a lot of our traffic is chatty and repetitive, that helps. but initial prefix-heavy summarization is mostly cold.
03:16 - Daniel: right, cold cache will hit you with higher per-token latency. we typically report cold vs warm p95s in the benchmark: cold can be 2-3x warm depending on KV size. we'll include that in the run.
03:30 - Ben: are streaming responses more expensive? we worried about token billing and performance with streaming.
03:38 - Maya: streaming still bills per-token but can improve perceived latency because tokens arrive incrementally. it can also increase network lines and concurrency management.
03:52 - Alex: how does Redwood do batching with streaming? does batching delay first token?
03:58 - Daniel: we use latency-aware batching. the runtime tries to batch but prioritize low-latency SLOs. first token can be prioritized via small batch windows; that's tunable. there's a practical tradeoff: lower batch windows increases cost.
04:20 - Tom: ok, next — we'd like a benchmark on our prompts. can you run a token/sec profile with our 50k sample tokens and the two model families we listed?
04:30 - Daniel: yes, we'll run a 2-hour throughput test across our Hosted and Dedicated config and report p50/p95/p99 for short and long responses, streaming throughput, and cold vs warm KV. we'll also capture per-request token counts and per-second aggregate token/sec.
04:45 - Priya: what's the expected time to provision Dedicated for the test?
04:50 - Maya: we can provision a small Dedicated pool in ~48 hours with our infra team if commit's there; for benchmarking we can spin a temporary dedicated slice in 24 hours in most cases.
05:02 - Sara: security question — how do you handle keys for Private? is there KMS integration with our HSM?
05:10 - Daniel: yes, Private supports KMS integrations and can point to your cloud KMS or HSM; keys never leave the customer's control plane. we'll attach the KMS checklist to the notes.
05:25 - Alex: do you do multi-region active-active? we want failover between us-west2 and us-east1 for latency spikes.
05:32 - Maya: yes, smart routing can route by region with automatic fallback. for strict p95 guarantees you'd want Dedicated in each region or a cross-region fall back policy with predictable increased latency.
05:48 - Tom: cost sensitivity — what's the primary lever? quantization, batching, caching?
05:54 - Daniel: all three. quantization reduces GPU memory and can increase throughput but may slightly affect quality; batching reduces per-token CPU overhead but increases latency for first tokens; caching (prefix/KV) is the biggest per-request win if you have repeated contexts. we'll produce a cost/latency sensitivity table in the playbook.
06:12 - Ben: any gotchas with streaming and TLS/long lived connections? we've seen connection churn hurts SLOs.
06:19 - Daniel: we recommend long-lived streams with keepalive and per-connection multiplexing. Redwood's runtime supports HTTP/2 streaming and we have reconnection semantics to resume KV where possible. but extreme churn will cause tail latency.
06:40 - Priya: for the benchmark, can you include a cold start profile when you scale from 0 to 200 concurrent calls?
06:48 - Daniel: yes, we'll include scale-from-zero and steady-state. that will show autoscaler spin-up time, queueing, and initial p95 hits.
07:00 - Tom: what's the actual expected p95 for short responses on Hosted with a 70B quantized model at concurrency 150? just to set expectations.
07:10 - Daniel: rough estimate: if network RTT is ~50ms, compute warm p95 might be ~220-300ms on a tuned runtime for short responses, so end-to-end could be in the 300-380ms range. that's under your 400ms but it's approximate — depends on your exact prompt shapes and batch profile.
07:32 - Sara: and for PHI, retention, do logs contain PII? we need auditability but masked logs.
07:38 - Imani (Redwood): we have token-level redaction options and audit log retention controls; we can produce a compliance mapping doc.
07:48 - Priya: are there any differences in model variants between Hosted and Dedicated? like quantization or kernel availability?
07:56 - Daniel: Hosted has a broad catalog with verified performance profiles. Dedicated can pin to a specific runtime and you can opt into custom quantization or kernel builds if you need. Private gives the most control but requires slightly more ops involvement.
08:15 - Ben: do you have any existing healthcare customers with similar SLOs?
08:20 - Maya: yes, we've run similar pilots; i'll redact names in the playbook but include anonymized profiles and numbers.
08:28 - Tom: ok let's walk through a sample flow — patient enters question, system calls model for 80 tokens, then follow-up summarization 600 tokens. how do you size capacity?
08:40 - Daniel: you'd size for peak concurrent requests * average token/sec per request, but also ensure headroom for bursts. for small requests prioritize low-latency pools (smaller batch windows, reserved capacity) and route heavy long jobs to separate workers or batch lanes to avoid head-of-line blocking.
09:05 - Alex: do you support route-level policies? like route A uses Dedicated, route B uses Hosted fallback?
09:12 - Maya: yes, routing policies can be per-route with fallback. common pattern: critical small latency paths on Dedicated, heavy async jobs on Hosted or separate Dedicated nodes.
09:25 - Priya: how will you measure aggregate token/sec? is it per-second sampling or sliding window?
09:30 - Daniel: we capture per-second aggregates with 1s resolution and sliding windows for 1m/5m/15m. we'll provide graphs in the benchmark output.
09:45 - Tom: noise — how much variance do you see across customers for p95?
09:50 - Daniel: variance usually comes from networking and workload shape. multi-tenant jitter is another factor; Dedicated reduces that. streaming has different tails than batch generation.
10:05 - Ben: anything on autoscaling policies? we are worried about scaling too slow and causing queueing.
10:12 - Daniel: autoscaler can be aggressively tuned: provisioned capacity, scale buffer percentage, and burst capacity. we can run a scale-surge test to validate.
10:28 - Maya: okay wrapping to logistics — we'll run the 2-hour benchmark; need your 50k token sample and two model choices (you listed gpt-like-67b and 13b equivalent).
10:40 - Priya: we'll upload the sample to the shared drive after this.
10:44 - Sara: also send over SOC2 and KMS checklists.
10:48 - Maya: will do. i'll attach Dedicated pricing ranges and the playbook deck to the follow-up email.
10:55 - Tom: timeline — we need numbers by early next week to decide pilot.
10:58 - Maya: we'll aim to deliver benchmark results and pricing by 2026-03-20.
11:05 - Imani: i'll schedule the 30 minute follow-up for 03/22, sending calendar invites.
11:12 - Ben: any concerns about PHI in test data we should avoid?
11:18 - Daniel: please scrub any direct identifiers; we can also accept synthetic tokens. for PKI/KMS specifics we'll handle with Sara.
11:30 - Tom: ok thanks everyone. good call.
